en: Verses in Praise of Amitābha Buddha, composed by Dharma Master Tánluán. *Namō Amitābha Buddha*.
Regarding the etymology of "Immeasurable Life" (*Amitāyus*), according to the *Bǎngjīng* (The Auxiliary Scripture), it is also called "Peaceful Nurturing" (*Ān-yǎng*).
Namo! With utmost sincerity, I take refuge and pay homage to Amitābha Buddha of the Western Quarter.
Currently residing ten trillion lands away from this world in the Land of Peace and Bliss, the World-Honored Buddha is named Amitābha.
I vow to be born there; I take refuge and pay homage.
Since attaining Buddhahood, ten kalpas have passed; his lifespan is now truly immeasurable.
The light-wheel of his Dharma-body pervades the entire Dharma-realm, illuminating the world’s blindness and darkness.
Therefore, I prostrate to the one of immeasurable wisdom-light; thus, the Buddha is also named Amitābha (Immeasurable Light).
All finite marks are illuminated by your light; therefore, I bow my head to you, the true wisdom of liberation, whose wheel of light is infinite and all-pervading.
For this reason, the Buddha is also called Boundless Light;
those touched by your light transcend both existence and non-existence. Therefore, I bow my head to the Equal Awakened One.
The clouds of light are unimpeded like space; therefore, the Buddha is also named Unobstructed Light.
All that is obstructed receives the luster of this light;
for this reason, I prostrate to the inconceivable, pure radiance that has no counterpart. Therefore, the Buddha is also named Peerless Light.
Those who encounter this light have the bonds of karma severed; therefore, I bow my head to the ultimate refuge.
The Buddha’s radiance shines most preeminently; thus the Buddha is also called King of Radiant Flames.
Those in the three dark realms of suffering receive the opening of enlightenment through his light; therefore, I prostrate to the Great Arhat.
The light of the Way is brilliant and its color transcendent; Therefore, the Buddha is also named Pure Light.
Once touched by this illumination, the stains of sin are removed, And all attain liberation;
therefore, I prostrate to the compassionate light that spreads afar and bestows peace and joy. Therefore, the Buddha is also named Joyful Light.
Wherever his light reaches, one attains the joy of the Dharma; I bow my head in prostration to the Buddha of Great Consolation.
His light can shatter the darkness of ignorance; Therefore, the Buddha is also named Wisdom Light.
All Buddhas and the assemblies of the Three Vehicles Unanimously praise him; therefore, I bow my head.
His radiance shines universally at all times; therefore, the Buddha is also named Uninterrupted Light.
Because of the power of hearing this light, the mind is never severed, and all attain rebirth;
thus, one prostrates to that light. None but the Buddha can fathom it; therefore, the Buddha is also named Inconceivable Light.
The Buddhas of the ten directions praise rebirth there, extolling its merits;
therefore, I bow my head to the divine light that is free from signs and beyond naming.
Because the Buddha is also named Unnameable Light, and because he attained Buddhahood through this light which shines brilliantly, and because it is praised by all Buddhas, I pay homage.
His radiance shines more brightly than the sun and moon; therefore, the Buddha is named "Surpassing the Light of Sun and Moon.
Even Śākyamuni Buddha could not fully praise him. Thus, I prostrate to the Peerless One;
may he take pity on me and protect me, causing the seeds of the Dharma to increase in this life and in future births.

May the Buddha always accept us with compassion; may we, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss. Homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss; may we, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss. Homage to Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss; may we, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss. Homage to the assembly of all pure Bodhisattvas of the great ocean-like multitude in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss; may we, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss. [I dedicate this] universally for my teachers, parents, spiritual friends, and all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm.
Having severed the three obstacles,
may we all together attain rebirth in the land of Amitābha Buddha.
We take refuge and repent.
The assembly of Amitābha Buddha’s first gathering— The number of śrāvakas and bodhisattvas is immeasurable;
Their supernormal powers and skillful means cannot be calculated.
Therefore, I prostrate to this vast assembly of great beings, Who enjoy peace and bliss, the infinite mahāsattvas, All of whom shall be born to succeed the Buddhas in their very next life.
Except for those who have made great vows of universal liberation to deliver all sentient beings—
these multitudes of merit from the Jewel Forest— I now join my palms with single-minded devotion and bow my head in homage to the śrāvakas of the Land of Peace and Bliss,
each of whom radiates light one fathom, like a falling star.
The Bodhisattva’s halo extends four thousand li; like the full autumn moon, he reflects the purple-gold light.
Having gathered the treasury of the Buddha-dharma for the sake of sentient beings, I therefore prostrate to this ocean of great resolve.
Furthermore, Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta are the most preeminent among all the assembly of sages.
The light of compassion illuminates the great trichiliocosm; attending the Buddha’s left and right, he manifests divine majesty.
He delivers all with whom he has a karmic connection without a moment’s rest, like the tide of the great ocean that never misses its time.
To this Great Compassionate One, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, I bow my head with single-minded devotion in prostration.
There are sentient beings born in peace and bliss, all fully endowed with the thirty-two marks;
their wisdom is perfected as they enter the profound Dharma.

Having thoroughly mastered the essentials of the Path without obstruction, they achieve patience according to the sharpness or dullness of their faculties—ranging from the two types of patience up to the incalculable.
Having always possessed mastery over the five supernormal powers throughout successive lives, Until reaching Buddhahood, you never again entered the evil realms;

Leaving behind birth in the five turbid worlds of other lands, You manifested in accordance with the Great Muni to be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss and achieve great benefit. Therefore, with a sincere heart, I prostrate my head at your feet.
The Bodhisattva Anle, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, traveled in the space of a single meal to incalculable Buddha-worlds throughout the ten directions.
There he reverently made offerings to all the Tathāgatas;
flowers, incense, and music appeared according to his thought, while precious canopies, banners, and pennants emerged at will.
Rare and marvelous, beyond this world, they cannot be named;
Scattered flowers and offerings of extraordinary jewels transform into flower canopies, their radiance dazzlingly bright. Their fragrance perfumes everywhere, reaching all without exception;
The smallest flower canopy spans four hundred li, While some even cover an entire Buddha-field.
Following their sequence, one after another, they passed away into transformation; all these Bodhisattvas were filled with joy.
In the void above, they played celestial music, elegantly praising his virtues and extolling the Buddha’s wisdom.
Having listened to the Dharma, received the teachings, and made offerings, they ascended into the air and returned before partaking of food.
Your spiritual powers are sovereign and unfathomable; therefore, I prostrate to the Unsurpassed Honored One.
The Bodhisattvas of the Buddha-land of Peace and Bliss can eloquently teach according to their wisdom;
Regarding all things, they have abandoned the notion of "mine," And are as pure as a lotus flower, unsullied by dust.
In coming and going, advancing and halting, you are like one drifting in a boat; Your sole concern is peace and security, abandoning likes and dislikes, self and other, as if they were empty.
Having severed these two notions, you kindle the torch of wisdom to illuminate the long night;
The three knowledges and six supernormal powers are all complete within you, And the myriad practices of a bodhisattva are threaded through your heart’s eye.
Such merits are boundless and immeasurable; therefore, with a sincere heart, I prostrate my head in homage to the assembly of śrāvakas and bodhisattvas who possess the voice of peace and bliss.
Their wisdom penetrates all things, both human and celestial, and their physical marks are adorned without distinction; they are listed here merely to accord with other regions.
His countenance is upright and peerless; his exquisite and subtle body is neither human nor celestial.
This body of emptiness is the infinite essence; therefore, I prostrate to the Power of Equanimity.
May all who are able to be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss abide entirely within the stage of those destined for enlightenment.
In that land, there are none who are fixed in error or indeterminate; for all Buddhas praise it, I prostrate to it.

All who hear the name of Amitābha Buddha, rejoicing with faith at what they have heard, and even those who for a single moment possess a sincere mind—should they dedicate their merit toward rebirth there, they shall all go thither.
Except for those who have committed the five heinous crimes or slandered the True Dharma, I therefore prostrate and pray to be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
To the assembly of Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas, and to Śākyamuni, whose great eloquence is unimpeded and beyond compare in this world—
I shall set forth various hypothetical suppositions to demonstrate even a small portion [of his merit].
The most lowly beggar is compared to an emperor, And the emperor is further compared to a Wheel-Turning King (Cakravartin).
In this manner, progressing through the stages up to the six heavens of the desire realm, each subsequent form is likened to the one preceding it as if starting from the beginning;
yet using the physical appearance of those celestial beings as a metaphor for the next, even a thousand million times [the former] does not equal the latter.
All these arise from the power of the vows of the Dharma-treasury; I bow my head in prostration to the Great-Minded One, the Deva among humans.

Whatever one may require, there is nothing that does not arrive according to one's wishes and thoughts—be it a single jewel, two jewels, or immeasurable jewels—manifested as articles for enjoyment in accordance with the mind.
The halls, buildings, food, and drink are all like this; Therefore, I bow my head to the Buddha of Ineffable Praise.

All those who have been reborn there are fully endowed with Pure physical bodies beyond compare, With supernormal powers, merit, and palaces, And their attire and ornaments are like those of the six heavens.
The precious alms-bowl, a vessel of merit, arrives spontaneously; In an instant, it is filled with delicacies of a hundred flavors.
Seeing their colors and smelling their fragrance, the mind takes them as food; Suddenly satiated, one experiences sublime joy.
The flavors tasted are pure and free from attachment; Once the task is done, they vanish, only to reappear when needed again.
Peaceful and joyful, next comes nirvāṇa; Therefore, with a sincere heart,
I prostrate my head before the Buddhas of the ten directions and their assemblies of bodhisattvas, As well as all the bhikṣus who have attained immeasurable,
innumerable, and incalculable peace and happiness— those born in the past, those born in the present, and those who shall be so in the future.
All have made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas and have grasped hundreds of thousands of steadfast dharmas;
such great beings are all reborn there. Therefore, I prostrate to Amitābha.
If one hears the name of Amitābha’s virtues, one shall joyfully praise and look up to him, taking refuge with a devoted heart.
Even if one attains great benefit for but a single thought-moment, one becomes fully endowed with the treasure of merit.
Even if the great trichiliocosm were filled with fire, one should pass straight through it to hear the Buddha’s name;
hearing the name of Amitābha, one shall never again fall back. Therefore, with a sincere heart, I prostrate in worship.
Amitābha of Infinite Spiritual Power, praised by the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions;
from the Buddha-lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the east, countless bodhisattvas all go there to pay their respects,
and likewise offer worship to the great assembly of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
Listening to and receiving the sutras and Dharma, proclaiming the Way and its transformation— just as it is in the other nine directions,
so too has Śākyamuni Tathāgata spoken these verses. Because of his immeasurable merit,
I pay homage to the immeasurable assembly of Bodhisattvas who have come here, reverently honoring them to plant the roots of virtue.
Some play music and sing praises of the Buddha; some extol the Buddha’s wisdom that illuminates the world;
some offer celestial flowers and robes as worship; and some, beholding the pure lands, give rise to vows of equality.
Thus the assembly of sages appears before them all, and they receive the Buddha’s prediction through his eightfold Brahma-voice.
All Bodhisattvas increase their vows and practices; therefore, I prostrate to the Bhagavān, the Holy Lord, the World-Honored One.
When the World-Honored One preached the Dharma, the great assembly gathered like clouds in the Hall of Seven Jewels;
hearing the Buddha’s instructions, they all attained realization, and with joy overflowing, they all attained the Way.
At that time, a pure breeze arose from the four directions, Striking the jeweled trees so they produced wondrous sounds;
Their harmonious and clear resonance surpassed the *xiuzhu* flute, Exceeding metal and stone instruments beyond compare.
Celestial flowers fell in profusion, following the fragrant wind, Spontaneously making offerings without ever ceasing.
The various devas further hold celestial flowers and incense, And employ hundreds of thousands of musical performances to pay homage.
Because of such merit, this assembly of the Triple Gem, I therefore direct my thoughts to worship the lecture hall;
This wondrous land is vast, transcending all numerical limits, Naturally composed of the seven precious jewels.
The Buddha’s power of original vows gives rise to adornment;
I bow my head to the pure and great gathering, whose world-light is wondrous and peerless.
Delightful and peaceful, beyond the four seasons, with the power of self-benefit and benefiting others perfected— I take refuge in the skillful adornment of expedient means.
The precious ground is serene and level as the palm of a hand;
though there are no mountains, rivers, hills, or valleys, through the Buddha’s spiritual power they appear whenever required. I prostrate to the Inconceivable Honored One.
The Bodhi tree is four million *li* high, with a circumference of fifty *yojanas*.
The branches and leaves are made of twenty thousand *bri* of cloth, naturally composed of various jewels;
it is adorned with the moonlight-mani ocean-wheel jewel, the sovereign of all gems,
and draped all around with precious necklaces of shifting colors in hundreds of thousands of varieties.
Its radiant flames shine forth, surpassing a thousand suns; Above it, infinite jeweled nets provide a canopy.
All manner of adornments appear according to conditions. I prostrate and pay homage to the Bodhi tree;
A gentle breeze stirs the branches, producing the sound of the Dharma, Which flows universally throughout the Buddha-fields of the ten directions.
Hearing this sound, one attains the profound Dharma-patience; until the attainment of the Buddha-way, one shall not encounter suffering.
His spiritual power is vast and immeasurable. I bow my head in prostration to the Bodhi tree, and to the trees of fragrance, color, sound, touch, taste, and the Dharma of the trees.
Those whose six sense-faculties encounter [the tree] attain the patience of dharmas; Therefore, I prostrate to the Bodhi tree.

Facing the Bodhi tree with the six faculties, Until the attainment of Buddhahood, the faculties become pure and clear, And sounds become gentle and compliant, as one realizes the patience of non-arising;
According to the depth or shallowness of their capacity, all obtain realization.
The majesty and power of this tree arise from the five kinds of powers of the Tathāgata,
his spiritual might, and the fulfillment of his original vows; its clear, firm, and ultimate vows, compassion,
and skillful means are beyond measure— I take refuge in and bow my head to this truly immeasurable one.

From the kings of the world up to the six heavens of the desire realm, the music becomes increasingly exquisite in eight successive stages, each surpassing the former by hundreds of millions of times.
The splendor of the jeweled trees and their sounds is likewise doubled;
furthermore, there are spontaneous and wondrous musical performances, with the pure and harmonious sound of the Dharma gladdening the mind and spirit.
Sorrowful, elegant, and resonant, transcending the ten directions; Therefore, I bow my head to the Pure Joy.
The groves of seven-jeweled trees surround the world; Their radiance is brilliant, mutually reflecting one another;
Flowers, fruits, branches, and leaves adorn each other. I bow my head to the mass of merit from original vows.
A pure breeze blows constantly upon the jewel trees, producing the five musical notes in harmonious and subtle resonance;
exquisite melodies are formed spontaneously.
Therefore, I prostrate to that pure land, which is perfumed and vast beyond all bounds, its surface entirely covered by nets of various jewels.
Adorned with gold threads, pearls, and rare jewels—treasures beyond description—it is embellished on all four sides with hanging precious bells.
When stirred by the gentle breeze, they emit the wondrous Dharma;
its elegant and virtuous fragrance flows forth constantly, so that those who hear it do not give rise to the habitual afflictions of worldly toil.
This wind touches the body and brings happiness, like a bhikṣu attaining the meditative absorption of cessation.
It blows through Buddha-fields filled with flowers; according to their colors, they appear in orderly sequence without confusion.
The substance of the flowers is soft and supple, emitting an intense fragrance. When one steps upon them, they sink down four finger-widths.
Whenever he lifts his foot, it returns to its former state; when his task is finished, the ground opens up and he vanishes without a trace.
According to the seasons, flowers bloom six times;
because his retribution is inconceivable, I prostrate to him who fills the world with lotuses of various jewels, each flower having hundreds of thousands of billions of petals.
The radiance and color of these flowers are immeasurable;
vermilion, purple, crimson, and green intermingle in five brilliant hues, shimmering and blazing with a brilliance that outshines the sun.
Therefore, with single-minded devotion, I prostrate and pay homage to the light emanating from each and every flower—light numbering thirty-six hundred billion times ten million.
Within each ray of light there is a Buddha-body; as many as the rays that have issued forth, so too are these Buddha-bodies, their marks and signs like mountains of gold.
Each one again emits hundreds of thousands of rays, universally preaching the wondrous Dharma throughout the ten directions, establishing all sentient beings securely upon the path to Buddhahood.
Such supernatural powers are boundless; therefore, I take refuge in Amitābha.
The pavilions and halls were not fashioned by craftsmen, but were produced through transformation from the seven precious gems, exquisitely carved and adorned.
There are canopies of interlaced nets with bright moon pearls as tassels, each accompanied by bathing pools whose forms correspond perfectly to them.
The eight meritorious waters fill the ponds, their color, flavor, and fragrance as pure as nectar.
The golden ponds have silver sands, and the sands of the seven-jeweled ponds alternate in this manner.
On the banks of these ponds, fragrant trees hang down and spread above, their sandalwood scent wafting with constant, exquisite perfume.
Celestial flowers in brilliant splendor serve as adornments; upon the water they shimmer like radiant clouds.
The fruit of dwelling in the state of non-outflow is inconceivable; therefore, I bow my head to the Bodhisattva Guṇakośa.
Śrāvakas enter this jewel pond, reaching depths according to their will, just as they desire.
If one requires ablution, water naturally pours forth; if one desires it to swirl back, the water immediately returns.
Its temperature is always harmoniously adjusted, neither too hot nor too cold. The spirit opens and the body rejoices as the mental impurities are washed away;
it is clear, pure, and limpid, appearing as if formless. Like precious sand reflecting light, it seems shallow though it is deep.
Gently swirling and turning, they pour one into another; Elegant and composed, they harmonize the human and divine spirits.
From these boundless ripples emerge wondrous sounds:
According to what is appropriate, some hear the Dharma teachings, Or the sublime verses of the Triple Gem, Or the silence of emptiness and non-self.
Some hear of the immeasurable *pāramitās*, the powers, the unique qualities, and the various supernormal knowledges;
some hear of the patience regarding non-action and non-arising, up to the dharma of the nectar-consecration.
According to their faculties, dispositions, and desires, they all rejoice, following the true meaning of the characteristics of the Triple Gem.
The paths traversed by Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas—of all these, he has heard them entirely;
the names of the sufferings and hardships of the three miserable realms are forever closed, and there is only the sound of spontaneous bliss.
Therefore, that land is named Sukhāvatī. With my head bowed to the crown, I pay homage to the Infinite Honored One.
Our original teacher, the Mahāsattva Nāgārjuna, was born when the principles of the Dharma were first collapsing;
he closed the gates of heterodoxy and opened the tracks of the True Path. He is the eye for all beings in Jambudvīpa;
I prostrate before the Honored One who has realized the Stage of Joy. I take refuge in Amitābha and am born in Sukhāvatī.
Just as when a dragon stirs, the clouds must follow, And when [the rain] falls upon Jambudvīpa, the hundred plants flourish;
Homage to the compassionate Nāgārjuna, I take refuge with a sincere heart and prostrate with my head at his feet.
Since beginningless time, I have wandered through the three realms, Spinning about within the wheel of delusion.
The karma created in a single thought-moment and a single instant is sufficient to bind one to the great earth and detain one within the three miserable realms;
I pray that the light of your compassion will protect and mind me, causing me never to lose the bodhicitta.
I praise the sound of the Buddha’s wisdom and merit; may those with karmic affinity throughout the ten directions hear it.
Those who wish to be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss, May all their aspirations be fulfilled without hindrance.
Whatever merit they possess, whether great or small, They dedicate it all so that everyone may be reborn together.
Namo to the One of Inconceivable Light; With single-minded devotion, we take refuge and prostrate.
The immeasurable wisdom of the ten directions and three periods of time, Riding together upon the one suchness, is named Perfect Enlightenment;
The path of the perfection of the two wisdoms is equal, Yet manifests in various ways to gather and transform beings according to conditions.
I take refuge in the Pure Land of Amitābha, Which is precisely taking refuge in the lands of all Buddhas.
With a single mind, I praise a single Buddha; May this reach all throughout the ten directions for those who are unimpeded.
Thus, to all the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions, I bow my head to each with a sincere heart.
May you take pity on me and protect me, Causing the seeds of the Dharma to increase In this life and in future births.

May the Buddha always sustain us; may we, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss. *Namo*, with a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss; may we, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss. *Namo*, with a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss; may we, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss. *Namo*, with a sincere heart, I take refuge and pay homage to the assembly of all pure great ocean-like bodhisattvas of the Western World of Ultimate Bliss; may we, together with all sentient beings, be reborn in the Land of Peace and Bliss. May this be for the sake of teachers, parents, spiritual friends, and all sentient beings throughout the Dharma realm.
Having severed the three obstacles,
may we all equally attain rebirth in the land of Amitābha Buddha.
We take refuge and repent.
